analysis.headline: Supreme Court Rules 6-3 for Trump on Asylum and TPS Cases
analysis.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court issued two major immigration rulings on Thursday, both decided 6-3 along ideological lines in favor of the Trump administration. In the first, the Court held that asylum-seekers who have not physically entered U.S. soil can be turned away without processing their claims, allowing the administration to revive a previously rescinded border-metering policy. In the second, the Court ruled that the president has authority to terminate Temporary Protected Status for Haitian and Syrian immigrants, clearing the way for potential deportation of hundreds of thousands of people.

context.significance: These two rulings represent the most significant judicial restructuring of U.S. immigration law in years, simultaneously contracting the legal pathways for both asylum and humanitarian temporary protection at the border and interior. The decisions entrench a legal framework in which presidential discretion over immigration enforcement is largely insulated from judicial review, shifting the balance of power away from courts and Congress in one of the most contested policy domains. For hundreds of thousands of Haitians and Syrians who built lives and livelihoods under TPS, the rulings mark an immediate and potentially irreversible change in status, raising urgent questions about mass deportations to countries still experiencing instability.
